structs.name: GfxTexture
structs.size_evidence: method 4 (array stride) + method 2 (deleting/release) + method 3 (whole-record writes). Texture pool slots are 64 bytes: R_TextureDesc_GetSlotPtr@0x140ee1210 returns &s_R_textureDescSlotTable[4*h] (__int128 units = 64 bytes per slot); R_TexturePool_AcquireSlotRetry@0x140edfdc0 counts 0x9080 slots with the bitmap at pool+2367512 = 16 + 36992*64 (the counter sits at pool+2367504); R_TextureDesc_IsSlotCurrent@0x140ee0180 and R_TextureDesc_ReleaseRecord@0x140ee1030 memcmp / write exactly 0x40 bytes, and ReleaseRecord writes four 16-byte resets (+0,+16,+32,+48). The game-test 48 is contradicted by the +56 store in R_TextureDesc_AllocateGpuResource@0x141937d50 (`*(QWORD*)(outResource+56) = v6`) and its release at +56 in ReleaseRecord. Replay max access end 64.
members: R_TextureDesc_GetSlotFieldU16@0x140ee1310 and R_TextureDesc_UnpackRecordFields@0x140ee1280 call the vtable at [*(slot+0)]+80 (a COM call, so +0 is a real interface pointer); R_TextureDesc_AllocateGpuResource@0x141937d50: `*(QWORD*)outResource = resourceHandle`; R_ReflectionProbeFiltering_SetupImageViews@0x141961480 calls `(*Resident)->vtbl+80` on the same pointer
R_TextureDesc_AllocateGpuResource: R_AssignNullShaderTextureView(outResource+8) (16 bytes); R_TextureDesc_ReleaseRecord: R_ReleaseShaderTextureView(record+8); game-test name and type confirmed

R_TextureDesc_CreateUavViews@0x141937a90: `R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView(outViews+24)` and `R_GfxRing_AcquireCopySlot(..., outViews+24)`; R_TextureDesc_ReleaseRecord: R_ReleaseShaderTextureRWView(record+24) and its test `(record+40) & 0xFFFFFFFB` (the RW view's +16 field). The view is 32 bytes (A187), so the IDA 24-byte pad is wrong

R_TextureDesc_AllocateGpuResource: `*(QWORD*)(outResource+56) = v6` (v6 is the heap block from R_Heap_DecodeBlockHandle / R_Heap_AllocateBlock); R_TextureDesc_ReleaseRecord: `if (*(record+56)) R_Heap_FreeBlock(*(record+56)); *(record+56) = 0`. Replay-only member, no game-test name; the name is descriptive, not game-test
changed_members: +56 heap block is written by R_TextureDesc_AllocateGpuResource@0x141937d50 and freed by R_TextureDesc_ReleaseRecord@0x140ee1030
unconfirmed: heapBlock name: descriptive only (the value is a heap block handle); the type unsigned __int64 is from the store width
basemap type: the COM vtable calls prove an interface pointer; the object's exact class (ID3D12Resource) is the game-test name, not re-proven here
structs.notes: The builder size 56 misses the +56 heap-block field. The Replay texture pool element is this 64-byte record (not a 48 or 144 entry), so GfxTexture is the slot itself. Pool holds 36992 slots (R_TexturePool_AcquireSlotRetry@0x140edfdc0) in s_textureGlob, which is a 2372140-byte object (16-byte header, slot table at +16 with 64-byte slots, counter at +2367504, bitmap at +2367512, next index at +2372136).

structs.name: GfxResidentTexturePoolEntry
structs.size_evidence: no separate wrapper type: the only Replay accessor of a resident texture is R_Texture_GetResident@0x140ee1420, which returns the 64-byte GfxTexture slot itself (`&s_R_textureDescSlotTable[4*h]` or the storage slot); its callers (R_ReflectionProbeFiltering_SetupImageViews@0x141961480, RB_BackendDataCopier_ExecuteCopyOp, R_ST_DispatchTerrainCompute, GfxLightmapAtlas_UpdateResidency) treat the result directly as GfxTexture (ID3D12 call at +0). No 48-byte array stride exists in the texture pool (the pool's only array is the 64-byte slot table, see GfxTexture). No Replay global or allocation of 48-byte texture entries was found.
structs.notes: game-test's resident entry is a one-member wrapper around GfxTexture at +0; in Replay the resident texture IS the GfxTexture slot, so this wrapper does not exist in this build. The IDA union GfxTexturePoolEntry (144 bytes, resident/streamed members) has the same problem: nothing in Replay uses a 144-byte pool element. That union is outside this entry (not in A207) and is flagged for the coordinator.

structs.name: GfxStreamedTexturePoolEntry
structs.size_evidence: no streamed-texture entry in Replay: the texture pool element is one 64-byte GfxTexture (see GfxTexture), so the game-test GfxTexture[2] + fallbackTexture (144/168 bytes) has no Replay storage. Replay's R_Texture/RB_Texture/Stream texture functions (full list of 46 R_Texture*/RB_Texture*/R_TextureDesc*/Stream_*Texture* names) contain no Streamed, Fallback, Move, Swap or CreateStreamedDefault function (the game-test R_Texture_Move / R_Texture_Swap / R_Texture_ResetFallback / R_Texture_CreateStreamedDefault / RB_Texture_AssignStreamedInternal do not exist here). Start_texture_update (495 bytes) has no texture stride (its only imul is `imul edx, [rbx+254h]`), R_UpdateResidentTexture@0x14189f240 only reads a texture-ref record at +80. RB_Texture_BeginAllowStreamedTextureUpdate@0x140ee00c0 just stores a context pointer.
structs.notes: The streamed fallback path is absent in this build. Replay keeps one 64-byte record per slot with a heap block at +56 instead. The IDA GfxTexturePoolEntry union that embeds this struct is not in A207 and is flagged for the coordinator.

structs.name: GfxReflectionProbeFilteringImageData
structs.size_evidence: method 5 (global extent) + method 4 (stride): three filter-state globals sit at 0x151101780, 0x151101A88 and 0x151101D90 (R_ReflectionProbeFiltering_Init and R_ReflectionProbeFiltering_Startup@0x141961ad0 pass them; SetupImageViews@0x141961480 and ShutdownImage@0x141961990 reach them through the same offsets). Each difference is 0x308 = 776 = 8 + 16*16 + 16*32. The view array begins at +8 (stru_151101788 = global+8) and the RW array at +0x108 = +264 (unk_151101888 = global+264). Builder size 776 is confirmed; game-test 648 and IDA 648 are contradicted.
members: SetupImageViews: `m_imageMipView` advances `++m_imageMipView` (16 bytes) and writes `->view` (+0) and `->resource` (+8, HIDWORD/LODWORD); ShutdownImage: `v4 = &stru_151101788; ++v4` releases each view

SetupImageViews: `m_imageMipRWView += 32`, writes +0 (resource), +8 (0), +16 (descriptor index), +20 (3), +24 (mip index v2), +28 (0); ShutdownImage: `v2 = &unk_151101888; v2 += 4` (32-byte stride) releases each RW view. Array size changed from 384 (16*24) to 512 (16*32)
changed_members: global stride 0x308 between the three filter-state globals
structs.notes: The RW view is 32 bytes (A187), so the element stride is 32 in both the loop and the global spacing. Shader view array length 16 is the game-test count and is consistent with the 776 stride.
